title: Simple Gifts
origin: Shaker dancing song written at the Alfred, Maine Shaker community in 1848

pd.detail: Joseph Brackett Jr. (1797-1882) wrote this Shaker dancing song at the Alfred, Maine Shaker community in 1848; Brackett died in 1882, more than 95 years ago, so both tune and setting are free worldwide.
pd.sourceEdition: The plain Shaker tune in D as it circulates in public-domain folk transcription; verified note for note and rhythm for rhythm against an independent ABC transcription in D (common time, 16 bars), which agrees on every pitch and every duration across all three strains.
pd.notes: Brackett's own 1848 words are carried on the three sung strains; see each section's lyrics.pd, which stands on the lyricist's dates independently of the tune's. What is encoded is the plain Shaker tune, NOT Aaron Copland's 1944 variations in Appalachian Spring and NOT Sydney Carter's 1963 Lord of the Dance adaptation, both of which are separate copyrights on the same melody. The tune is duple and is printed in both 2/4 and common time; the consulted transcription is in common time and its 16 bars map one to one onto the 16 bars encoded here, so no note value or bar rate is changed. The two-eighth low-5 pickup is carried on the last beat of the preceding section, per the song book pickup rule. Verse, Bridge and Turn are the source's own three strains; the two-bar Intro is editorial, built from the tune's own closing phrase, not extra tune. Note the melodic variant: some hymnal transcriptions give the second bar as 5-5-5-3-2-1, where the consulted D-major folk setting and this encoding have 5-5-4-3-2-1.

pd.detail: Brackett (1797-1882) wrote the words as well as the tune at the Alfred, Maine Shaker community in 1848; he died in 1882, so the text is free worldwide on the lyricist's own dates, not merely the composer's.
pd.sourceEdition: Wikisource transcription of Brackett's original 1848 Shaker verse (tagged PD-old), which is the same single verse Copland set in 1944.

lyrics.notes: Brackett's original verse is the whole song; the three later non-Shaker verses in circulation are not his and are not carried. The tune is eight two-bar lines, so the four lines here fall on bars 0, 2, 4 and 6. Each line after the first is preceded by a two-eighth low-5 anacrusis on the last beat of the previous bar (beats 7.5, 15.5 and 23.5 of this section); the line is pinned to the downbeat bar its stressed syllable lands on, matching how line 1 is pinned to bar 0 with its own pickup carried in the intro.

stanzas.text: 'Tis the gift to be simple, 'tis the gift to be free
'Tis the gift to come down where we ought to be,
And when we find ourselves in the place just right,
'Twill be in the valley of love and delight.

lyrics.notes: Two two-bar lines, as everywhere else in the tune. Line 1's eight syllables run from bar 0 to beat 6; the rising 1-2 eighths at beats 7 and 7.5 are the anacrusis on 'To bow', so line 2's stressed syllable lands on the downbeat of bar 2.

stanzas.text: To bow and to bend we shan't be ashamed,

lyrics.notes: The closing couplet. One stanza only: Verse, Bridge and Turn each play twice in the form and sing the same words both times, since Brackett wrote a single verse.

stanzas.text: To turn, turn will be our delight,
Till by turning, turning we come round right.
